requirements.requirement: The system must successfully ingest distance_miles and duration_minutes from Google Routes responses and persist them in the proximity score object during unit tests.
The system must compute a normalized_score between 0 and 100 for a valid set of trials and assert all values fall within this range.
The system must validate that normalization produces relatively higher scores for shorter distance/duration trials compared to longer ones within the same result set.
The system must return proximity score fields (distance_miles, duration_minutes, normalized_score, metadata) in the API response via evaluate_care_facade.
The system must ensure API responses conform to the schema defined in clinical_trials_models.py for proximity data.
The system must include route_source and timestamp metadata in proximity results and validate their presence in integration tests.
The system must correctly handle a zero distance case (user location equals trial location) and assign the highest normalized_score in the result set.
The system must correctly process long-distance outliers and ensure normalization does not produce negative scores or exceed 100.
The system must return a consistent number of trials before and after proximity enrichment in integration tests.
The system must preserve original trial identifiers and core fields when adding proximity data in API responses.
The system must handle missing user location input by returning proximity fields as null or omitted without causing service failure.
The system must handle missing or incomplete Google Routes data by skipping scoring for that trial and not breaking the full response.
The system must ensure deterministic scoring results for identical inputs across repeated test runs.
The system must validate that integration tests cover both unit-level scoring logic and facade-level API response assembly.
